reason: The GUI's harness activity panel can stop a harness-native subagent task and rewind files to a checkpoint, and its artifact inspector reads, searches and saves a tool call's retained output; the terminal could only list activity and results. /activity in a harness conversation now offers Stop subagent for tasks Core marks stoppable (when the profile advertises subagent_control) and Rewind files to a checkpoint (only when the profile advertises checkpoint_rewind and the session is idle), and /results browses retained results with an artifact inspector: read numbered lines with Core's line or long-line continuation cursor, search all output of a tool call with Core's match cursor, and save the raw output after acknowledging sensitive data. Selected: the new inspect unit suite against Core's documented shapes, the workflows, shell and TUI suites (the /activity and /results paths and command text), the client wheel allowlist, a real-Core PTY journey on a paired TLS LAN Core, the product-knowledge search and Chroma digest sync, and the settings-catalog terminal test.
exclusions: No full suites. No native or Playwright changes: only the separate Python terminal client, docs and settings catalog keywords changed, and the catalog change is covered by its Vitest file. tests/test_terminal_pty.py and tests/v3/test_terminal_core.py are not selected because several of them fail identically on pristine origin/main; they were run locally against a merge of the round-2 terminal branches and against pristine origin/main; the same tests failed on both, apart from two intermittent ones described in the PR (one of which also fails intermittently on main). The inert real-Core fixture has no tool artifacts, native subagent tasks or checkpoints, so those actions are covered by the unit suite. No live provider calls or Core deployment.
